reason: Re-opened packet.js pali 6: Story VI.1 (A Poor Man Wins Spiritual Treasure, Norman [106] to [107]) has the Teacher say verbatim that a monk shown a fault ought to be amenable to discipline like Radha and should not take offence when admonished, and that he who gives admonition should be looked upon as one who points out where treasures are to be found, then speak verse 76; the paraphrase follows it clause for clause. Radha is Sariputta’s pupil in the story, so the pupil Radha is right. The Pali Tattha agrees (kopo na kātabbo, tuṭṭheneva bhavitabbaṃ). Plain sense true: 76 opens chapter VI, The Wise Man, and speaks of whom to follow. verse.js ok (Dhammapada 76, at 75); entry-check ok.
